records.label: Two infertile sisters from a consanguineous family
quotes: we identified a homozygous missense mutation (c.895T>C; p.C299R) in TBPL2 (TATA box binding protein like 2) in two infertile sisters with oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration from a consanguineous family by whole-exome sequencing.

records.label: 32-year-old infertile woman

phenotypes.hpo_label: Elevated circulating follicle stimulating hormone level

phenotypes.text: two failed oocyte collection attempts / failure of superovulation

quotes: A 32-year-old female was diagnosed with unexplained primary infertility for 10 years. She had roughly normal basal hormone levels, but her basal follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels were elevated.
In addition, the level of anti-Mullerian hormone was within the normal range, and she had undergone two failed oocyte collection attempts.
One novel mutation, c.802C > T (p. Arg268Ter), and one known variant, c.788 + 3A > G (p. Arg233Ter), in TBPL2 were identified in the infertile family.

records.label: FinnGen women homozygous for TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter
quotes: with women carrying two copies of the risk allele having an average of only 0.16 (SD = 0.58) offspring. According to the registry data, only four homozygous women for the TBPL2 mutation had children, and all of them had received infertility treatment

two out of 41 individuals carrying two copies of the risk allele had given birth to one child, whereas two individuals carrying two copies of the risk allele had given birth to more than one child. All four women had undergone IVF therapy

notes.statement: In a GWAS of 22,849 Finnish women with infertility and 198,989 control women from FinnGen, Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) used a recessive model and identified a genomewide-significant association with a nonsense variant in TBPL2, c.895A>T (p.Arg299Ter). The odds ratio was 650.1 (p = 4.11 x 10(-25)).
quotes: The strongest association was observed in the recessive analysis at the TBPL2 locus on chromosome 14 with an odds ratio (OR) of 650.1 (p = 4.11 × 10−25).

Our recessive analysis identified a low-frequency stop-gained mutation in TATA-box binding protein-like 2 (TBPL2; c.895A>T [p.Arg299Ter]; minor-allele frequency [MAF] = 1.2%) with an impact comparable to highly penetrant monogenic mutations

notes.statement: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that the TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter variant had a minor allele frequency of 1.1% in Finland. This was 43 times higher than in non-Finnish Europeans. Allele frequencies were fairly even across Finland, ranging from 0.84% to 2.38%.
quotes: is a rare stop-gained mutation (p.Arg299Ter, minor-allele frequency [MAF]: 1.1% in Finland) that is highly enriched to Finland (43 times compared to non-Finnish Europeans). The variant appears rather evenly distributed across Finland, with an allele frequency range of 0.84%–2.38%

notes.statement: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that women homozygous for TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter had an average of 0.16 offspring, compared with 1.75 in the other genotype groups. All homozygous women who had given birth had received infertility therapy, including IVF. In a phenome-wide analysis, the variant was associated only with infertility.
quotes: individuals carrying two copies of that variant having significantly fewer offspring (average of 0.16) compared to women belonging to the other genotype groups (average of 1.75 offspring, p = 1.4 × 10-15). Notably, all homozygous women who had given birth had received infertility therapy.
In our follow-up analyses, the TBPL2 mutation was associated only with infertility and no other diseases.

notes.statement: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) confirmed that the TBPL2 locus acts recessively: the proportion of women with infertility was significantly raised only among those carrying two copies of the effect allele.
quotes: These data confirm that both the PKHD1L1 and TBPL2 loci exhibit a recessive mode of action, i.e., the proportion of affected individuals with infertility is significantly elevated only among individuals carrying two copies of the effect allele.

notes.statement: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) noted that p.Arg299Ter introduces a premature stop codon in the DNA-binding part of TBPL2. It is predicted with high confidence to be a loss-of-function variant (CADD score 40), and the authors expected it to significantly impair transcription of downstream targets.
quotes: The mutation introduces a premature stop codon (p.Arg299Ter) in the DNA-binding part of the protein predicted to be a high-confidence predicted loss-of-function variant (pLOF) with a Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) score of 40 (www.gnomad.org) and can hence be expected to significantly impair the transcription of the downstream targets.

notes.statement: Du et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing in an infertile woman with impaired ovarian folliculogenesis and identified compound heterozygous TBPL2 mutations: a novel nonsense mutation (R268X) and a known splice variant (c.788+3A-G). They confirmed the mutations by Sanger sequencing and proposed that they caused the patient's impaired folliculogenesis, failure of superovulation, and infertility.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing was performed on the patient, and TBPL2 mutations were identified and confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
We identified compound heterozygous mutations in TBPL2 that caused impaired ovarian folliculogenesis, failure of superovulation, and infertility in patients.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2021) reported that the homozygous TBPL2 p.C299R variant was rare and pathogenic, and that it impaired the transcription initiation function of the protein.
quotes: The TBPL2 mutation is rare and pathogenic, and impaired the transcription initiation function of the protein.

notes.statement: Yang et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing in 2 unrelated infertile families with oocyte maturation defects and found a homozygous splicing variant (c.788+3A>G) in the TBPL2 gene. A minigene assay showed that the variant disrupted the integrity of TBPL2 mRNA. Haplotype analysis indicated that the disease alleles in the 2 families arose independently.
quotes: A homozygous splicing variant (c.788 + 3A>G) in TBPL2 was identified in two unrelated families characterized by oocyte maturation defects. Haplotype analysis indicated that the disease allele of Families 1 and 2 was independent. The variant disrupted the integrity of TBPL2 mRNA.

notes.statement: Yang et al. (2021) performed single-oocyte RNA sequencing on 2 immature metaphase I (MI) oocytes from patients. Genes vital for oocyte maturation and fertilization were widely and markedly downregulated, which the authors suggested meant that mutation of the transcription factor TBPL2 led to global gene alterations in oocytes. They noted that direct functional evidence was lacking.
quotes: Transcriptome sequencing of affected oocytes showed that vital genes for oocyte maturation and fertilization were widely and markedly downregulated, suggesting that a mutation in the transcriptional factor, TBPL2, led to global gene alterations in oocytes.
only two immature MI oocytes were obtained from the patients

notes.statement: He et al. (2020) reported that a recurrent mutation in the TBPL2 gene causes diminished ovarian reserve and female infertility.
quotes: A recurrent mutation in TBPL2 causes diminished ovarian reserve and female infertility.
